resolution.quote: Adding EIGEN_MAKE_ALIGNED_OPERATOR_NEW to class declaration solves the problem  (corot, comment 18128700, same day as the fix; commits verified this session: 18b46dc and its cherry-pick f62c63f, both 'Issue #257: 32 bit alignment Eigenlib error', adding '+  EIGEN_MAKE_ALIGNED_OPERATOR_NEW' to the Bumper2PcNodelet class in kobuki_bumper2pc/include/kobuki_bumper2pc/kobuki_bumper2pc.hpp)

notes: Sources opened this session: issue 257 body (stonier, 2013-05-15: the Eigen DenseStorage.h:69 assertion, the '[FATAL] ... Service call failed!' lines and the mobile_base_nodelet_manager death with exit code -6, all verbatim) and the comment thread (corot's 'Case 1' diagnosis, his later ecl/auto-docking comments 'The root of the problem remains, but now it's an ecl problem.'); both fix commits' diffs. Eligibility agree: the consumer's plugin object embedding fixed-size vectorizable Eigen members is allocated with new without the 16-byte-alignment macro, and the misaligned address handed to Eigen's constructor crosses the library API boundary — a wrong value/timing crossing the boundary with the resolving edit inside the consumer, which the tree counts as an interface failure; the failure depends on the pairing (32-bit malloc plus Eigen's documented requirement), so step-2 internal is not available; PAIR and library API fit. LOUDNESS agree: Eigen's own assertion (naming the violated requirement and its documentation URL) fires from existing tooling while the nodelet manager constructs the plugin during the nodelet load service call — loud_documented/activate is the same pattern CAL2-01 uses for the robot_model ROS_ERRORs. TWO DISAGREEMENTS: (1) CLASS — the spec's failed_conditions[0].class is 'representation_convention', but that class covers 'component or byte order, handedness, or encoding of a value crossing the boundary'; a memory-alignment ABI precondition is none of these, and the spec's own notes state 'no class in the list fits exactly; recorded as other' — the JSON field again contradicts its own notes (same defect pattern as CAL2-01). Proposed: 'other'. (2) RESOLUTION — the spec records 'observed', but 'observed' requires the source to show the resolved composition working with both units identified by revision; corot's 'solves the problem' is a maintainer statement without the Eigen revision of the test machine (the spec's own evidence text concedes this), and jorge's ROS Answers confirmation ('We fixed it and released just now...') lives on answers.ros.org, which was unreachable this session. The packet's own CAL2-02 spec applied exactly this stricter standard to an identical pattern (maintainer confirmation without revisions -> recommended). Proposed: 'recommended'.
